title: Overview

heading: Step 1. Add a New Layer
body:
There are four types of layers: drawing layers, image layers, dimensions layers, and text layers.

Drawing Layers
Tap the Add Drawing Layer button to create a new drawing layer. Layers in Trace have boundaries and are not infinite, just like real sheets of trace paper. They're also the size of your current screen view. If you want to increase your drawing area, you can zoom out and add a new layer.
text:
Layers > Overview :: Step 1. Add a New Layer

There are four types of layers: drawing layers, image layers, dimensions layers, and text layers.

Drawing Layers
Tap the Add Drawing Layer button to create a new drawing layer. Layers in Trace have boundaries and are not infinite, just like real sheets of trace paper. They're also the size of your current screen view. If you want to increase your drawing area, you can zoom out and add a new layer.
title: Overview

heading: Pro Tip If you want higher resolution while zooming in simply zoom in to the area you are drawing and add a layer. As long as you draw on that zoomed in layer, you will see improved resolution.
body:
Image Layers
Tap the Add Image button to add an image to your drawing. You can resize, crop, and place your photo.

Paste Images from Photos
You can also add an image layer by copying the image in Photos. Then long press anywhere in your project area and a "Paste" button will pop up. Tap "Paste" to paste in your image.

Dimension Layers
Tap the Add Dimension button to add a dimension layer to your drawing. You can set the precision, size, and color of your dimensions. You can add multiple dimensions to the same layer as well as override the text in each dimension.
Learn more about Dimension Layers >

Text Layers
Tap the Add Text button to add a line of text to your drawing. You can set the font, size, and color of your text. You can add multiple text boxes to the same layer so you only need one layer for all of your text.
Learn more about Text Layers >

Delete all drawings from the layer. This action canbe undone and redone.

Delete

Built directly into Morpholio, AI Scale simplifies your project setup. By reading the scale of your imported drawings, it calibrates your tools for you without compromising your privacy or control of the design process. In seconds, you can start sketching with precise dimensions, rulers, and Smart Fill for areas and hatching.

AI Scale is built on Apple's VisionKit which means that despite the magic, your projects never leave your device and predictions are generated from the iPad or iPhone’s own processors, not data centers. It’s local AI with a narrow scope and a daily benefit.

heading: Step 1. Show Grid & Enter Set Grid
body: Tap the Wrench button and then "Scale". Toggle "Show Grid" on to make your rid visible. Next, tap "Set Grid" to enter grid edit mode.

Tap the Wrench button and then "Scale". Toggle "Show Grid" on to make your rid visible. Next, tap "Set Grid" to enter grid edit mode.
title: Scale Grid

heading: Step 3. Align Your Grid
body: Drag the Cross-Hair to align the origin of your grid with an existing drawing. Alternatively, you can tap the Cross-Hair to align the grid to a corner, edge, or the center of your base layer.

Drawing & Scale Tools > Scale Grid :: Step 3. Align Your Grid

Tap the Color Circle to change the color. Adjust the slider on the bottom to change the opacity. When your grid is set, tap the Green Check to apply your changes and start drawing!

body: To snap your lines to the grid, tap the wrench icon, select "Grid" and then toggle on "Show Grid" and "Snap to Grid." Now, when you draw lines near the grid, they will auto-snap to the straight lines along the grid, even if you do not have your ruler turned on.

heading: Step 3. Select Your Lasso Type
body:
Choose the Lasso Type at the bottom that works best for your selection scenario.

Freeform
Use the Freeform Lasso option to select around irregular curved shapes. Drag your Pencil to create a freeform curve selection.

Polygon

Circle/Ellipse
The Circle/Ellipse option is best for circular quick selection. Press and drag your Pencil to create a circular selection.

Square/Rectangle
The Square/Rectangle option is best for rectangular quick selection. Press and drag your Pencil to create a rectangular selection.

heading: Step 2. Set Vanishing Points
body: If it’s your first time opening perspective tools in your project, you’ll automatically be pushed to choose One-, Two-, or Three-Point Perspective. You can then drag the Cross-Hairs to set your vanishing points. Vanishing points can be positioned over a blank page, site photograph, or model to start your drawing.
text:
Perspective Tools > Overview :: Step 2. Set Vanishing Points

If it’s your first time opening perspective tools in your project, you’ll automatically be pushed to choose One-, Two-, or Three-Point Perspective. You can then drag the Cross-Hairs to set your vanishing points. Vanishing points can be positioned over a blank page, site photograph, or model to start your drawing.
title: Overview

heading: Step 3. Assisted Perspective Drawing
body:
After you set your vanishing points, Trace will automatically create a perspective grid for you to draw on top of. You can use the "Guide" tool to draw specific lines along your perspective grid. Tap the Gear button to open your perspective settings and set up your perspective tools. Try out different combinations of the tools below to get your perfect setup.

Grid
Show or hide the perspective grid.

Guide
Drag the Guide Circle to the location where you want to add your lines. You can then use your Pencil to draw lines along the guidelines.

Assist
Automatically draw towards a vanishing point from anywhere on the page.

title: View Setup

heading: Step 1. Pick Your Camera Mode
body:
Choose between Orbital, Ortho (orthographic), and POV (Point of View) camera modes.

Orbital
This is the most popular mode to set exciting perspectives from all angles. In this mode, panning with one finger orbits your view around the 3D model.

Ortho
This mode will help you set up great plans and elevations of your 3D model.

POV (Point of View)
This mode is great for interior perspectives and for capturing a view at eye level. It operates from a first-person perspective. In this mode, panning with one finger rotates your camera around as if you were moving your head to look around the space you're in.

Orbital

Ortho
This mode will help you set up great plans and elevations of your 3D model.

POV (Point of View)
This mode is great for interior perspectives and for capturing a view at eye level. It operates from a first-person perspective. In this mode, panning with one finger rotates your camera around as if you were moving your head to look around the space you're in.
title: View Setup

heading: Step 2. Set Your Camera
body:
Simple gestures help you pan, zoom, orbit, and reset your camera to capture the best view.

Orbital Gestures
Use these gestures to navigate while in Orbital mode.

1 Finger Tap to set the center of focus.
1 Finger Double Tap to reset the camera to its original position.
2 Finger Pinch to zoom the camera in and out.
1 Finger Drag to orbit the camera around your center of focus.
2 Finger Drag to pan the camera across your view.

Ortho Gestures

1 Finger Double Tap to reset the camera to its original position.
2 Finger Pinch to zoom the camera in and out.
2 Finger Drag to pan the camera across your view.

POV Gestures

1 Finger Tap to set the center of focus.
1 Finger Double Tap to reset the camera to its original position.
2 Finger Pinch to zoom the camera in and out.
1 Finger Drag to rotate the camera and "look around".
2 Finger Drag to pan the camera across your view.

Use RoomPlan to scan any room effortlessly to create a scaled 3D model, set your view, and sketch over it instantly. Create plans, elevations, perspectives, axons and so much more!
title: RoomPlan

heading: Important Note If your screen is gray and not displaying the view below, you likely need allow Trace to access your camera. Go to the Settings App , scroll down to Trace , and then toggle on "Allow Trace to Access Camera" .
body:
Apple Tips for Scanning
Follow these guidelines provided by Apple for the best experience with RoomPlan.

Model: Melissa Velarde

A. Scan only residential or small commercial spaces
RoomPlan works best with ceiling heights less than 12’ and in rooms that are not larger than 30’ by 30’.

B. Scan one room at a time
Complete the scan for a single room before you move onto the next one.

C. Prep your space
You’ll get the best scan when the corners of the room and the edges of windows are visible. You should also close your doors so the scan knows where to end.

D. Conditions to avoid
The following conditions may disrupt your scan:

- Scanning at night or in spaces that do not have daylight
- Full-height mirrors or glass
- Ceilings above 12'
- Dark surfaces and poorly lit corners
- Scanning the same area over and over
- Scans that last over 5 minutes

title: Drawing Export

heading: Step 2. Select File Type
body:
You can choose between PDF, image, PSD, Vector, or Project.

PDF
Export a layered PDF with each layer that you choose to share as a separate PDF page.

Image
Export an image of each layer that you choose to share as a separate image.

PSD
Export a Photoshop file with each layer as a separate layer in your file. If you select this option, skip to Step 5. Take note that the extent of this file is defined by the base layer. Anything outside of the base layer boundary will not be exported.

Vector
Export a Vector-based DXF file with each layer as a separate layer in your file. Move your Trace plans into CAD, sketches into 3D, or elevations into your favorite design software. However you use Trace, it just got a lot easier to take your hand drawings to the next level. If you select this option, skip to Step 5. Learn more here >

Project
Export a fully editable file for use on another device or as a backup. If you select this option, skip to Step 5.

body:

Arrange Your Page
Tap one finger on the layer preview. Then, drag one finger to reposition the drawing.

Edit Sheet Title & Number
Tap on the sheet title or sheet number to edit.

Export
Toggle which layers you want to export.

Print Size
Select the sheet size for each layer exporting. This does not change the layer size inside your drawing.

Print Scale
Select the sheet scale for export. Keep this as "Screen" to keep the scale set in your drawing. Note that this does not change the scale of your layer inside your drawing.

Borderless
Toggle the white border on or off.

Layers
Display all other layers on the sheet.

Titleblock
Show your titleblock on the sheet. You can change the name and company image for your title block in your Settings.

heading: Step 5. Resolve a File Conflict
body:
If you see a yellow cloud icon on your project, don’t worry! You likely have the same project open on two devices and iCloud is trying to save both versions at the same time. You can resolve the conflict and save all of your important work. Here’s how:

First, tap on the conflicted project and select "Resolve Conflict."

Then, select which version of the file you want to keep on all devices and tap "Keep Selected." If you want to save both versions, just select "Keep Both."

Your settings help you configure your default workspace. Once you have the perfect setup, you can always come back to adjust the details. These pro settings help make Trace the best app for architecture.
Does your interface look different? Make sure you have the latest update for Trace here.
title: Overview

heading: Step 1. Set Up Your Apple Pencil
body:
While any stylus will give you basic functionality with Trace, Apple Pencil gives you the most advanced stylus experience.

Pencil Only Drawing
Turn this on to activate palm rejection and avoid making marks with your palm or finger.

One Finger Pan
Turn this on to pan around your drawing with one finger.

Double Tap Behavior to Show Ruler
Quick switch between free hand drawing and straight line drawing with the ruler by turning this on.

Left-Hand Mode
Left-handed users can toggle this on to switch the positions of your layer toolbar and your pen toolbar.

Layer Background Color
Set the background color of the layer toolbar. Use "Transparent" when making a drawing with white lines on a dark background to see your linework.

heading: Step 2. Define Your New Project Default Settings
body:
These settings will be applied to any new project you create. You can override these settings for an individual project by adjusting the settings inside the wrench in a project.

﻿
Default Units
You can set your default units to imperial or metric. This will adjust your ruler, triangle, protractor, area calculator, dimensions and more.

New Layer Color
Set the color for new layers that you add to a drawing.

Default Units

title: Overview

heading: Pro Tip If you change this to the Blank option (red strike-through), you will avoid getting a 50% opacity layer added to every project that you create.
body:
Layer Drop Shadows
Turn this on to view a subtle drop shadow around the boundary of each layer. This will not export when you share your drawing.

Stack Layers
If you'd like all of your new layers to be the exact size of your base layer, turn "Stack Layers" on. If you keep this off, all new layers will be the size of your current view.

Edit Images
Turn on to use the Eraser and Lasso with images.

Tool Color
Change the color of your ruler, triangle, protractor, and stencils.

PDF Slider
Show or hide the PDF Slider for navigating quickly between pages in your PDF.

Show Line Length
Turn this on to see the length of your line as you draw.

Hold to Straighten Line
When this is on, you can hold your Pencil after you draw a stroke to turn it into a straight line.

Undo/Redo Gesture
Toggle this on to use a two-finger tap to undo and a three-finger tap to redo. If you toggle this off, you can only use the undo and redo icons in the pen toolbar to undo and redo your actions.

Zoom Rotation Lock
Toggle this on if you prefer to always keep your sheets upright without rotating as you zoom in and out.

Rotation Snap
Snap tool and layer rotations at 45º and 90º.

Why Subscriptions? At Morpholio, our goal is to always continue to add and improve features, while still keeping TracePro affordable for as many people as possible. Thus, based on your many requests, we offer a multiple subscription options. This allows everyone from beginners with a single project to pros with unlimited work to enjoy the app at an affordable rate. Instead of an expensive one-time license, the subscription model gives everyone access to continuously updating professional design software at a fraction of the cost. This also allows users to get only the tools and features they need and, if they desire, can always upgrade their subscription over time.

In addition, one subscription will now give users full access across all their devices. With TracePro, your subscription not only gives you both iPhone and iPad together, you'll also have access to updates, new tools, community events, special educational tools, and personal email support whenever you run into a challenge.

This section below will help you understand, access and manage your subscription made though the Apple App Store to meet any of your specific needs.
